---
title: "Avg_GRM_MinMax"
description: "Combines the two: high relationship to the target and low relationship within the training set."
---

Combines the two: high relationship to the target and low relationship within the training set.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Relationship |
| Direction | Larger is better |
| Uses a test set | yes |
| Score a given set | `avg_grm_minmax_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "AvgGRMminmax")` |

## Definition

$\mathrm{Avg\_GRM}(T,P) - \mathrm{Avg\_GRM\_self}(T)$. Without a test set the target is the candidates left out of the training set.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
avg_grm_minmax_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "AvgGRMminmax",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain

# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "AvgGRMminmax", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Fernández-González, J., Akdemir, D., & Isidro y Sánchez, J. (2023). A comparison of methods for training population optimization in genomic selection. *Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 136*, 30. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-023-04265-6>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** Code of Fernández-González et al. (2023): [github.com/TheRocinante-lab/Publications](https://github.com/TheRocinante-lab/Publications/tree/main/2022/Fernandez-Gonzalez_et_al_2022_Comparison). Package TrainSel: [github.com/TheRocinante-lab/TrainSel](https://github.com/TheRocinante-lab/TrainSel).
